data.name: Metamorphic
data.detailed_description:
Darkness. Falling. Light. A metallic, geometric cavern surrounds you. A single source of light beckons you forward, up – towards the only exit.

Inspired by Portal and Minecraft, Metamorphic is an atmospheric, first person physics-based puzzle game, which lets the player absorb, configure and then morph non-gravity, gravity and antigravity cubes to complete each level.

Key Features:
  • Procedural voxel, physics-based gameplay
    Metamorphic's core mechanic is the first of its kind. Each puzzle requires the player to assemble configurations of static cubes, select and then transform them into physics-affected objects. Any three dimensional arrangement you can conceive will then be accurately influenced by gravity and friction.

  • It's about solving puzzles
    Most first person platformers require the player to execute moves with pinpoint accuracy and timing such that solving the puzzle is rarely the hardest part, Metamorphic requires nothing of the sort. Despite the fact that the game is physics based, each puzzle simply requires the player correctly arrange and transform voxels to progress.

  • Skill development based
    Metamorphic will test your understanding of physics unlike any other game. While levels can be completed quickly if their solutions are known, each section of every puzzle requires the player to make a leap in their comprehension of the underlying system keeping the game from feeling repetitive or tedious.

  • Atmospheric Environment
    Beautiful lighting, reflections and sounds immerse you in each intricately designed chamber.

reviews.review:
Metamorphic is a first person puzzle game where you have to collect and place coloured blocks to create platforms to bypass obstacles and reach higher ledges. White blocks stay where you place them, green blocks fall down unless there's something solid underneath them, red blocks rise up unless there's something solid above them.

I like this genre. I've played several excellent games, including the Portal series, Talos Principle, Qube and Qbeh. Unfortunately, Metamorphic is a terrible game, and I regret buying it. I was actually close to refunding it, but I could see there weren't many levels remaining, so I thought I might as well finish it.

It only took me 3 hours to finish the game, which is far too short. Puzzle games will usually give you some basic puzzles to introduce the key concepts, and then build the difficulty up with increasingly more complex puzzles. Metamorphic gives you a few basic puzzles, and then just when you feel like you're ready to tackle the more complex stuff, its all over. You'd probably expect to see lots of puzzles where the solution requires you to use the different coloured blocks together in interesting ways, but I only remember that happening a couple of times.

Most of the time the solutions are pretty obvious, but the thing that slows you down is the physics. These blocks have curved edges, so they tend to move around when you stand on them. It can get a bit frustrating when you've built a structure that should allow you to cross a gap or reach a ledge, and then just as you're about to do the final jump, the whole thing collapses and you have to rebuild it.

The control system is ridiculous. To place blocks you first have to left click to place an outline, then hold Q and left click again to select the outlined blocks, and then press E to make them solid. That's right, you have to press 3 different buttons to place a block. Maybe its a good thing that the game was short, because that's quite annoying. Also, you can't change any of the key bindings. On a PC game in 2016. This is unacceptable. Furthermore, there's a post on the forum dated 9th July where the developer says key rebinding will be added in a couple of days. Its now December, so that was a lie.

Finally, this game is SO buggy. Here's a list of all the bugs I encountered in my 3 hours of gameplay.
- On the first green block puzzle, I initially couldn't figure out how to place the blocks. They were just outlines that I couldn't stand on. After consulting a Youtube video, it turns out a tutorial message was supposed to pop up on screen to explain the controls. It never appeared for me, even though "show tutorials" was definitely ticked in the options menu.
- Every time (and I mean, literally, EVERY time) I finished a level and was walking towards a train that takes you to the next level, the game would freeze for a second while it loaded in the next area. All forward movement stopped, and I had to release and repress the W key to carry on walking. I remember a similar bug happening in another game recently (it might have been Killing Floor 2?) and it was patched within a day.
- On two occasions near the end of the game, after I died and respawned, I was unable to collect or place blocks. It was like the game had stopped responding to mouse clicks. I had to quit to the main menu and reload the level.
- After the end credits finished and I returned to the main menu, the mouse cursor was gone and I couldn't interact with any options, including the one to close the game. I had to kill the game on the task manager. It actually seemed quite fitting that my very last experience in this game would be a bug.

If you're considering purchasing this game, don't. There are so many better games to choose from.
